key_insight: ESPINN can infer both the bulk chemical potential and gradient coefficients in phase-field models from limited transient snapshots using physics-informed pseudo-spectral learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-efficient way to identify constitutive laws for phase separation and microstructure evolution when physical parameters are unknown.
method: Uses an extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural network (ESPINN).
Jointly reconstructs free-energy structure and gradient terms from snapshot data.
Applies the framework to inverse identification of the 1D Cahn-Hilliard equation.
evidence_signal: In noiseless tests, the method accurately and stably recovers parameters from even a single snapshot pair, while noise reduces accuracy but more snapshots improve robustness.
watch_item: Performance degrades under noisy observations, so practical deployments will need careful denoising, snapshot selection, and uncertainty handling.
paper_title: Extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural networks for phase-field models
